extracted.intended_audience: readers and buyers interested in journalism, media studies, political science, and academic libraries (students, scholars, and journalists)
extracted.subtask_description: Commercial product/detail page for an academic book about the news media's role in politics, containing publisher/product metadata, a descriptive blurb, editorial reviews, and buying options. The page is aimed at potential purchasers and readers (including students, instructors, and researchers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thesis: news media as political institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Argues that the news media are in fact a political institution integral to the day-to-day operations of the three branches of our government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cook goes beyond claims about press impartiality to demonstrate how the media are structured as an institution that exercises collective power and how the role of the media has become institutionalized within the political process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated influence on policy and political action
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows that media do more than reflect politics: they affect policy and instigate, rather than merely reflect, political actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book argues newsmaking and governing are inseparable and gives examples of institutionalized media roles (e.g., press offices everywhere) to support claims about media influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / argumentative novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Presents an innovative thesis that challenges journalistic lore and political myth by treating the media as political institutions and their operatives as political actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note the work 'flies in the face' of common assumptions and offers a novel contribution to understanding media; the book 'goes far beyond the single claim that the press is not impartial.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Research quality / evidentiary basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterized as 'meticulously researched' with historical grounding and careful documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library Journal summary: 'Cook begins historically, summarizing how the nascent federal government used postal regulations...' — the book uses historical evidence and prior scholarship to build its case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical rigor / tight argumentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers praise the logical structure and reasoning of the book, indicating rigorous analysis rather than polemics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical value / suitability as course text
rubrics_metrics.description: Useful as a supplemental text for courses in media history, media management, and for journalism instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer recommendation: 'This book should be read by journalists . . . by mass communication faculty teaching courses in media structure or effects and journalism faculty as a supplemental text...' and 'Recommended for academic libraries.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability / audience suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone and style are relatively academic and 'rather dry,' making it less suited to casual readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library Journal notes: 'this rather dry work is tightly argued... casual readers will find little evidence of that tension here.' Indicates the book is aimed more at academic/professional audiences than general-interest readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical contextualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a historical account of the formation and evolution of the press, starting from the early days of the republic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book traces how newspapers were sponsored by political parties and how practices (like postal regulations) shaped the press, using historical narrative to support institutional claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to scholarship / impact on the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Considers the book an innovative contribution that advances understanding of the media's role in politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer endorsements (e.g., 'innovative contribution to our understanding of media') highlight the work's scholarly significance and potential influence on future research and teaching.
